properties.decision:
`snapshot_node` skips edges whose other endpoint is a bookkeeping node type, and `DesignEpoch` is on that list. Anthony's call 2026-07-31, of three offered: FIX IT by excluding on the edge's own role — a named `COMMITMENT_EDGES` list holding `SCHEDULED_FOR` — rather than leaving the epoch as the only route or deferring it to separate work.

THE PROXY WAS EXACT WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN AND STOPPED BEING SO. Every edge to a `DesignEpoch` used to be audit trail (`AT_EPOCH`, `OCCURS_DURING`), so excluding the endpoint type excluded the role, and the rule read as correct because it WAS correct. `SCHEDULED_FOR` broke it: an edge to an epoch is now a COMMITMENT — when this was due — which is design content by any reading, and `req:intent-preserved` says the past is never overwritten.

WHAT IT COST WHILE IT HELD, and why this is a defect rather than a preference: `record_change` on a scheduled requirement — the obvious, natural way to record "this slipped" — captured a snapshot with the schedule edge silently dropped. The old due date was destroyed by the very call whose entire job is preserving it, and the call REPORTED SUCCESS. Only the epoch-side snapshot preserved it, and nothing said so. The trap `dec:arrival-delta` named was therefore worse than stated: it is not merely that re-pointing an edge loses the slip, it is that the correct-looking remedy lost it too.

The audit trail it travels with is still excluded, and a test pins that: `AT_EPOCH` on the same node stays out. Role, not endpoint.

REJECTED: leaving it, with the epoch-side snapshot documented as the only route — the obvious wrong route would stay silently lossy, and a convention that has to be known is not a property. REJECTED: taking it as separate work — it is the substrate the arrival delta reads, so building the delta on a lossy capture would have shipped a report whose inputs quietly disagreed with each other.
properties.name: A snapshot excludes by edge ROLE, not by endpoint type — a commitment to an epoch is design content
properties.rationale:
FOUND BY READING THE CODE THE DECISION DEPENDED ON, not by a detector — and nothing could have flagged it. A snapshot that drops an edge is indistinguishable from a snapshot of a node that never had one: there is no second, contradicting fact to make the loss computable. That is the same blind spot recorded in `dec:epoch-pins-a-version-combination` ("a single edge pointing the wrong way creates no cycle and trips no detector"), one layer down — here it is an edge's ABSENCE from a record, which is even quieter than a wrong edge's presence.

The general shape is worth keeping, because this project keeps meeting it: a rule that was exactly right for the vocabulary existing when it was written, and became wrong when the vocabulary grew, WITHOUT anything changing at the site of the rule. `BOOKKEEPING_TYPES` was never edited; `SCHEDULED_FOR` was added somewhere else entirely. Proxies decay silently when the thing they proxy for moves.

Mutation-checked: empty `COMMITMENT_EDGES` and `a_schedule_edge_survives_a_snapshot_of_the_item` fails, while the epoch-side test keeps passing — which is also the evidence that the two routes were genuinely asymmetric before this.
